subject.title: Add plan-first Claw status and remove

question: Should OpenClaw sponsor this experimental core Claws status/remove and durable ownership-provenance contract after final real-world cleanup proof, or keep the stack limited to non-destructive planning until the RFC direction is settled?
rationale: The implementation introduces new destructive CLI behavior and persistent lifecycle semantics across a still-open RFC and stacked prerequisite PRs; correctness checks cannot decide whether this belongs in core or which recovery contract OpenClaw should permanently support.

options.title: Sponsor with final proof
options.body: Approve the core lifecycle direction once an exact-head redacted terminal proof covers each referenced-resource cleanup mode and the stack’s recovery semantics are reviewed together.

options.title: Keep status and planning only
options.body: Defer destructive removal while retaining read-only visibility and plan generation until maintainers settle the persisted ownership contract.

options.title: Pause the lifecycle stack
options.body: Leave the experimental series unmerged until the RFC chooses a different ownership or cleanup boundary.

recommendation.title: Sponsor with final proof
recommendation.body: Approve the core lifecycle direction once an exact-head redacted terminal proof covers each referenced-resource cleanup mode and the stack’s recovery semantics are reviewed together.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent shared-state, configuration, and filesystem-boundary work makes them the strongest available decision owner for the core persistence and destructive-operation boundary.
